summary: Initial security posture discovery for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for latency-sensitive financial workloads. Customer concerned about SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and data retention/residency. Agreed next steps: share compliance docs, network checklist, and schedule PoC scoping.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we can jump in. i'm jordan from redwood, AE, with maya our solution eng. little bit of context, we do these sec posture calls to map reqs to hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:18] Alex Rivera: thanks jordan, i'm alex, cto at silverstream. priya is our head of security, sam is devops. we're evaluating options for low-latency inference for transaction scoring, sensitive pii in tokens, so security is top.
[00:30] Priya Singh: hi all, quick note — compliance is a must, we need SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 evidence, also strong audit trails and KMS integration.
[00:40] Maya Patel: absolutely. just to surface, redwood's hosted environment is SOC2 covered, and we have iso certs — i'll share links — for customers with stricter reqs we support dedicated reserved capacity and private deployments with VPC and customer-managed KMS.
[00:56] Alex: okay can you clarify the differences in terms of data access? for hosted, do you have any plaintext stored?
[01:05] Maya: hosted does not persist customer request payloads beyond retention windows unless configured for logs/analytics; we treat embeddings and generations as ephemeral by default. however, for pci/regulated workloads customers typically opt for dedicated or private so they can control network egress and key management.
[01:24] Sam Wu: on KMS, can we use our aws ksm — sorry, aws k m s — to manage keys so redwood cannot decrypt? we prefer customer-managed keys.
[01:33] Maya: yes, in private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. for dedicated we offer integrations with customer KMS in certain configurations — there are some limitations with hosted where we manage keys for tokenization and caching, so that's a tradeoff.
[01:48] Priya: what about encryption at rest for models and kv cache? critical for us.
[01:53] Maya: models in hosted are stored encrypted and kv cache is encrypted at rest; for guaranteed separation and audit we recommend private with customer-managed key so you hold root-of-trust.
[02:07] Alex: audit logs — do you provide immutable audit logs, and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[02:13] Jordan: yes we have audit logging across control plane ops and request metadata. we can stream logs to customer SIEM via syslog/s3 connectors and we keep an immutable write-once log for a configured retention. i'll surface the retention defaults and options.
[02:27] Priya: retention is important — our legal team needs 7 years for certain transaction records. does redwood allow arbitrary retention windows?
[02:35] Maya: retention ranges depend on deployment: hosted has standard retention tiers (30/90/365 days) for request logs; dedicated and private can be configured longer since you control log shipping and storage. seven years is typically done via exporting logs to your long-term storage.
[02:50] Sam: ok network wise, for private we need vpc peering or private link and no public internet egress. can you support that?
[02:58] Maya: yes private supports VPC peering and interface endpoints; we can do single-tenant on-prem packages too. we'll share a sample network diagram and required firewall rules.
[03:08] Alex: SSO — we use okta, scim for provisioning. how mature is your SSO/SAML and SCIM support?
[03:15] Jordan: full SAML2.0 SSO supported, SCIM provisioning for users is supported in dedicated and private; hosted also supports SAML and SCIM but enterprise features like fine-grained RBAC map more cleanly in dedicated/private.
[03:30] Priya: how about role-based access control — can we define granular roles, restrict access by project or environment?
[03:36] Maya: yes RBAC with project-level roles, admin/read-only/ops roles, token scoping; in private you can integrate with your IdP for groups to enforce least privilege. there are some UI caveats on hosted where some org-wide features are bundled.
[03:50] Alex: do you do penetration testing and vulnerability scanning?
[03:54] Jordan: yes annual pen tests and regular vuln scans; we can share summary reports and remediation timelines.
[04:00] Priya: about certifications — can you share your SOC2 report and ISO 27001 certificate under NDA?
[04:06] Jordan: yes i'll send SOC2 type II artifact and iso cert, plus standard sec questionnaire.
[04:12] Sam: any limitations on model artifacts — do you accept customer-provided models? we'd like to host a fine-tuned model behind redwood.
[04:20] Maya: we support customer model onboarding in dedicated/private; hosted we have curated models only for managed infra but we can discuss custom model hosting in dedicated.
[04:30] Alex: can we run evals and benchmarks against latency SLOs? we need p99 under 150ms for short seq.
[04:36] Maya: we support performance benchmarks; for p99 under 150ms we'd likely recommend a dedicated pool or private co-located infra; we can run a pilot and share perf spreadsheet.
[04:48] Priya: regarding data residency, our customers in eu require eu-only processing. can you guarantee region locking?
[04:55] Maya: yes region locking is available in dedicated/private and hosted regional deployments; we'll note regions and data residency commitments in the spec we send.
[05:06] Alex: what about logging of prompt/response payloads — are they considered PII if we send customer names?
[05:12] Jordan: we classify request payloads as potentially containing pii, and by default hosted strips/stores minimal telemetry; for full control you should use private so you own the logs and storage.
[05:24] Priya: small question on legal — do you offer data processing agreements and addendums for data subject requests?
[05:31] Jordan: yes DPA available, we have standard DPA and can add data residency and processing terms for enterprise contracts.
[05:38] Alex: pricing tradeoff quick note — dedicated looks more expensive but gives us isolation; any burst options?
[05:45] Maya: dedicated supports burst capacity and reserved pools, there's also intelligent batching/optimizations to reduce token costs; optimize team can help shape config for latency vs cost.
[05:58] Priya: ok risks — can you talk about detection/alerting for anomalous request patterns or exfil attempts?
[06:05] Maya: we have integrated anomaly detection and tracing hooks, plus per-route alerts; in private you can plug into your SIEM for customized detection.
[06:16] Alex: next steps, sounds like: share SOC docs, network diagram, retention options, and schedule PoC scoping.
[06:23] Jordan: yep i'll send SOC2 and iso links, maya will share network checklist. when can we do the deep-dive? week of 3/23?
[06:31] Alex: that works. thanks everyone.
[06:34] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and invite.
[06:38] -- end of recording --
